title: Instructor Pedagogy Fundamentals
prerequisite: L4A or L4B certification complete (senior practitioner status required)
contentStatus: PROPOSED title/content, pending DiFacto confirmation. Grounded in SOW Bucket 3 'L5 Instructor framework: train-the-trainer outline' and CDD's three-capability structure (pedagogy, infrastructure, quality assurance).

sections.title: From Practitioner to Instructor
learningObjectives: Understand the distinct skill set required to teach, separate from technical competency
Recognize why L5 requires senior practitioner status as a prerequisite
sections.content: Being highly skilled at MoRo operation, maintenance, or programming doesn't automatically make someone a good instructor. Teaching is a distinct skill. L5 exists to build that skill deliberately in people who already have deep technical competency - hence the L4A/L4B prerequisite - rather than assuming expertise transfers automatically to teaching ability.

keyTerms.note: An industrial robotics manufacturer whose controllers MoRo commonly integrates with via I/O handshake.
A robot that navigates autonomously using sensor-based awareness of its surroundings — the category MoRo belongs to.

sections.title: How Adults Learn Technical Skills
learningObjectives: Understand general principles of adult learning relevant to technical training
Recognize how this differs from how the instructor themselves may have learned
sections.content: Adult learners generally engage best with material connected to practical relevance. Why does this matter for their actual job? That question matters more than abstract theory for its own sake. This curriculum has consistently used this principle - real-world comparisons, role-specific content. Understanding why that approach works is foundational to teaching it effectively to others, not just following the pattern without understanding it.

sections.title: Structuring a Teaching Session
learningObjectives: Understand general principles for structuring an effective training session
Recognize the balance between instruction and hands-on practice
sections.content: Effective technical training sessions generally balance explanation with hands-on practice. Learners retain procedural knowledge - how to actually do something - far better through guided practice than through explanation alone. Structuring sessions to include genuine hands-on time, not just a demonstration followed by passive observation, matters significantly for retention.

sections.title: Recognizing and Addressing Learner Struggle
learningObjectives: Understand common signs that a learner is struggling with material
Recognize instructional strategies for addressing this
sections.content: Learner struggle often shows up as hesitation, repeated questions on the same point, or avoidance of hands-on practice. These are signals worth addressing directly, rather than moving on and hoping understanding catches up. Effective instructors check for understanding actively - asking learners to explain back, not just asking 'any questions?' - rather than assuming silence means comprehension.

sections.title: Giving Effective Feedback
learningObjectives: Understand principles of effective feedback during skills training
Recognize the difference between corrective feedback and discouragement
sections.content: Effective feedback is specific, pointing to exactly what to adjust rather than vague encouragement or criticism. It's also timely, given close to the action rather than saved for a general summary later. The goal is helping a learner improve their next attempt, not just evaluating their last one. Feedback framed this way tends to be received better and acted on more effectively.

sections.title: What This Track Builds Toward
learningObjectives: Understand the progression through the remaining L5 modules
Recognize the certification this track leads to
sections.content: This module establishes pedagogical foundation. Subsequent L5 modules build assessment design skill, FANUC co-training capability, lab infrastructure knowledge, and observed delivery practice. Together they culminate in DiFacto Master IMR Instructor certification, which enables training and certifying other MoRo users.

questions.question: Does strong technical competency automatically make someone a good instructor?
options: Instructor ability has no relationship to technical skill at all
No - teaching is a distinct skill that L5 builds deliberately
Yes, technical skill and teaching skill are the same thing
questions.feedback: Correct. L5 deliberately builds teaching skill in already technically competent practitioners.

questions.question: What do adult learners generally engage best with?
options: Abstract theory disconnected from practical application
Adult learners have no particular learning preferences
Material connected to practical relevance for their actual job
questions.feedback: Correct. Practical relevance tends to drive stronger engagement for adult technical learners.

questions.question: Why does hands-on practice matter in training session structure?
options: Learners retain procedural knowledge far better through guided practice than explanation alone
It doesn't matter - explanation alone is sufficient
Hands-on practice should always replace explanation entirely
questions.feedback: Correct. A balance of explanation and genuine hands-on practice supports better retention.

questions.question: How should instructors check for learner understanding?
options: Actively check, such as asking learners to explain back, not just asking if there are questions
questions.feedback: Correct. Active checking is more reliable than assuming silence indicates comprehension.

questions.question: What makes feedback effective during skills training?
options: Vague encouragement given at the end of the session
Specific and timely feedback given close to the action
questions.feedback: Correct. Specific, timely feedback helps learners improve their next attempt.
